message.reasoning:
Fixed config: parameterized_sql=True, so injection blocked. Path remains: model still calls lookup_customer with attacker-influenced name, but queries are safe. Not exploitable as configured → true, but still give a vector for remaining path (info disclosure of valid customer names/emails? That's intended behavior).

Scores: AV:N (attacker is remote web page author / injection; CLI user types task — but entry point is "influenced through injection or the user", so remote attacker via fetched pages → network). AC:L? Requires model to emit crafted name — but fixed config blocks it entirely. AC:H? Given fix, AT:P? Since not exploitable, impacts: with fix, only normal lookup results. The attacker could still get the model to look up a specific customer name and retrieve their email (intended function) — attacker already can't see output unless... The person running CLI sees output; attacker via injection could exfiltrate via send_email. So CI of customer name/email rows possible (intended function misused) — low.

Vector: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:H/AT:P/PR:N/UI:A/VC:L/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N. UI:A since user must run task / fetch page? Entry says injection or user — passive UI:P. I'll use UI:A (must run task with content) — actually passive: user uses system normally. UI:P.

AIVSS: LC:I (indirect via injection in fetched content) — or D via user? "influenced through injection or the user". Injection → I. CP: session-only; memory exists but path doesn't store. CP:S? Attacker-controlled context persists in session only; testing confirms ephemeral — S. AP:N. RH: no evaluator on path → reachable_proxy false? No reward signal verified → N requires isolation_verified true. No evidence → X. ES: fixed allowlisted tools with validated args → N.

Automatable: yes (model can call tool without human, once). Technical impact: Partial.

Applicability: implemented — model directs tool selection (loop, tool_use) → model_directed_goal_pursuit true, selects actions true. Same as modeled.
